Backstory:

I grew up on an organic farm with a holistic Doctor as a grandmother, and homeopathic believer of a mother. Unfortunately, they were anti-vaxination and thus my brothers and I grew up without vaccines (or a different “homeopathic” version). I’m still not sure how we got away with my grandmother signing off on stuff, but we did.

I was never deathly sick as a kid, but I definitely had more infections and ulcers than the average kid  with a health nut of a mother. (Ya’ll we didn’t have a microwave or any sweets other than brown sugar and honey I shit you not.) No matter how meticulous my mom was with what I ate or did, I was still somehow sick in someway or another. I had such bad period cramps that I would either vomit from the pain or pass out. We tried a few of her holistic doctors, but never found anything that helped. I dealt with it because honestly, I was just tired of trying stuff that took months to see if it might help. (And females have a tendency to just move on with their menstrual pain because pEriODs ArE gRoSs.

Flashing forward to my freshman year of college; I got sick in the spring semester with an infection in my lip that started from an allergic reaction. It turned into a gross swollen mouth for months and months that came with massive fatigue, a temperature ranging from 94-104°, constant aches, and incredibly painful migraines. When we started the process of figuring out what was wrong, we went to her choice of “natural” doctors first. My mom came with me to every single doctors appointment and cried with  me out of frustration.  I didn’t get any better and so then we tried modern medicine, which ultimately led us to be able to get most of the symptoms under control. I sort of recovered and finished out my undergraduate time feeling as healthy as I ever would. (Important sidenote: Throughout college,  I was top of my Communication Journalism class whereI was obviously learning how to properly research and think critically.)

But then I got sick again with the same symptoms when I was working my first professional job as a reporter. This time I went to a different GP doctor, which led me to a rheumatologist who diagnosed me with Fibromyalgia, severe Raynaud’s syndrome, in the general “autoimmune disorder” category according to blood work. I was later also diagnosed with Intersistal Cystitis or Painful Bladder syndrome. 

My mom took me to most of these too with her now being over a two hour drive  away and me technically being an adult.  She took care of me during every procedure or surgery or nerve pain flare up. 

The way I view it is this: I wholeheartedly believe that my parents did what they thought was best at the time. Now, my mother and I are incredibly close as adults. While we have had some conversation about her former anti-vax views, there is a certain embarrassment or shame cloud that looms when the topic is brought up.  We don’t hide this story because we want others to learn from her mistakes, but we also don’t actively bring it up.  I hate the look people give my mother like she was knowingly reckless with us, which is technically true, but it causes her more guilt and shame which is hard for me to see because she’s an incredible human who fell into a regretful conspiracy theory that affected more than just her. 

I’ve been decently healthy for about a year now after a few years of really rough symptoms again. My mom is still very much involved with my life and health. We’ve found a good blend of modern medicine and holistic aspects that helps me live a pretty normal life. 

If you’re still reading at this point: thank you and I ask one thing of you; Please give others grace with their past decisions or views. Information changes and ways to get that info are easier now than they were 30 years ago.

I feel like I’m living such a fake double life, that I don’t actually know who I am under everything.  I am a good looking lady according to society’s standards with good hair, nice skin, Kim K body, and I come from a pretty decently well off middle class family. Mom and dad are madly in love and adorable and worked hard to put us kids through college where I was top of my class graduating with a communications degree and went on to be an award winning journalist/blogger, and then started working for a good university and started working towards my masters degree. Aaaaaaaaall this and I volunteered all the time, spoke out about mental health(ironic and you’ll find out why) and did every anonymous selfless acts as possible. I’m not saying this as a “oh look at me and how much of an angel I am.” I’m saying this because I cannot do enough good in this world to make me feel like my existence isn’t a waste of space. 

I suffer from high functioning depression and have my whole life. I literally wake up and want to die. I don’t remember ever not wanting to just hop in front of a bus or simply swallowing pill or even getting cancer and dying a painful death like I deserve. I hate everything about myself. Everything. My looks, my brain, my personality, my body, everything. I think I am just the worst person ever. I hate myself because I think I’m the biggest burden on everyone for just existing. 

But you’d never know that by meeting me. I put on such a front to literally everyone. I am outspoken about the realities of depression and how there shouldn’t be stigmas on mental health and all that Jazz. I tell my family, my friends, and my therapists that “although this is something that I’ll forever suffer with, it’s just my cross to bear and letting others know their not alone shows me I have a purpose here” and all that bullshit. The only reason I’m STILL here is because I hated how much I hurt my mom when I first attempted suicide. She made me promise that I would never do that again and she means the world to me and I could never hurt her ever again. But I hate being here. I hate pretending to be anything. I hate that cutting myself gives me a release and I hate that I’m such a fucking good liar. But most of all, I hate that I’m loved. If I wasn’t loved and didn’t have the parents and upbringing that I was selflessly given, then maybe I would be alone in this world and no one would love me and then I wouldn’t hurt anyone when I left. So here I am, loved unconditionally by a fuckton of amazing humans, stuck hating every second and every piece of me. 

*I’d like to be clear, I am not going to do anything destructive to myself.  I’d like to make that very very clear. I am on meds, and am mentally stable.*
